module.purpose: Provides a deterministic conversion from a 22-byte Uint8Array into a 24-character padded base64-like nonce string for web application use.
module.summary: This module defines a base64 alphabet and exposes a synchronous transformation that validates a 22-byte input, masks each byte into base64-compatible values, applies a narrower mask to the final two bytes, and appends two padding characters. Invalid-length input produces an empty string.
module.businessContext: Supports generation or representation of web build nonces used in application security or cache/build identification. Failure yields an empty nonce and may invalidate downstream nonce-based behavior.
functions: buildNonce (~L8-46): Converts 22 bytes into a padded 24-character base64-like nonce.

units.name: buildNonce

detail.name: buildNonce
preconditions: BASE64_ALPHABET is available and supports charAt(index).
postconditions: For an input of length 22, returns a 24-character string ending in "==".
For an input of length other than 22, returns the empty string.
invariants: The first 20 byte values are masked with 0b111111 before alphabet lookup.
The final two byte values are masked with 0b110000 before alphabet lookup.
The output contains one alphabet character for each of the 22 input bytes, followed by "==".
edgeCases: An empty Uint8Array returns the empty string.
Any Uint8Array whose length is not exactly 22 returns the empty string.
A 22-byte Uint8Array is accepted, including bytes with values across the full Uint8Array range.
For the final two bytes, only bits selected by 0b110000 affect the alphabet indexes; the lower four bits are discarded.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Returns an empty string when uint8array.length is not exactly 22.

detail.ioFormatSpec: Returns either an empty string or 22 base64-alphabet characters followed by exactly two '=' padding characters, for a total length of 24 characters.
detail.summary: Builds a 24-character nonce string from exactly 22 random bytes by mapping masked byte values through the base64 alphabet and appending two padding characters. Returns an empty string when the input does not contain exactly 22 bytes.

specLiterals.role: Selects the first 20 bytes for six-bit masking; the final two bytes use the alternate mask.
Masks the first 20 bytes to six bits before base64 alphabet lookup.
Masks each of the final two bytes before base64 alphabet lookup.
Required two-character padding suffix for the returned nonce.

specTests.then: The result is exactly the empty string.
The result has length 24, ends with "==", and its first 20 characters use indexes byte & 0b111111 while its final two characters use indexes byte & 0b110000.
